1//! Bounded, sharded key→partition-offset cache (issue #1570, Epic B/B4).
2//!
3//! The Cassandra **key-cache** analogue: a small LRU that maps a partition key to
4//! the location the index/trie descent produces, so a repeated hot point read can
5//! seek straight to the partition and skip re-walking `Index.db` (BIG) or the
6//! `Partitions.db` trie (BTI). B1's [`DecompressedChunkCache`] caches decompressed
7//! *chunk bytes*; this caches *locations* — immutable facts about an immutable
8//! SSTable, never row data (rows change shape under projection).
9//!
10//! # Design (see `openspec/changes/key-partition-offset-cache/design.md`)
11//!
12//! - **Keyed on the FULL raw partition-key bytes** (D1): the correctness guardrail
13//!   is "a cache hit returns the SAME location a fresh lookup would." Hashing the
14//!   key to a `u64` would admit collisions → a hit could return a *different* key's
15//!   offset, so the LRU is keyed on the owned key bytes (`Box<[u8]>`), collision-free
16//!   by construction.
17//! - **Per-reader** (D2): a location is meaningful only within one SSTable's offset
18//!   domain, so each reader owns its cache. Invalidation is trivial — the cache dies
19//!   with the reader on remove/reload (the audit's "SSTables are immutable, evict by
20//!   sstable identity" rule), so there is never a stale-location hazard.
21//! - **Sharded `Mutex<Shard>`, APPROXIMATE-BYTE bounded** (D3): `LruCache::get`
22//!   mutates recency (hence a `Mutex`, not an `RwLock`), hand-sharded (power-of-two,
23//!   masked) so the hit path locks exactly ONE shard, never a process-wide lock —
24//!   B1's concurrency rule. Each shard is an `LruCache::unbounded()` whose resident
25//!   footprint is bounded MANUALLY by an approximate-BYTE budget (not a raw entry
26//!   count), mirroring B1's [`DecompressedChunkCache`]. Partition keys are
27//!   variable-length (composite/text, up to Cassandra's ~64 KB), so bounding by
28//!   entry *count* would NOT bound resident *bytes* — a count cap of 4096 with
29//!   worst-case ~1 KB keys across ~40 readers is ~160 MB, breaching the `<128MB`
30//!   budget. Bounding by bytes makes the aggregate footprint independent of key
31//!   size (see [`DEFAULT_KEY_CACHE_BYTES`]). Each shard's bucket array still grows
32//!   only with actual occupancy, so an idle/empty reader's cache costs ~nothing.
33//! - **Resolution-hit only, never a MISS** (D4): the cache stores only a location a
34//!   lookup actually resolved, never a definitive MISS, so it can never fabricate a
35//!   hit for a key the underlying structure did not resolve. Both read paths preserve
36//!   the correctness guardrail (a cache hit returns the SAME location a fresh lookup
37//!   would, so any downstream check reaches the identical conclusion), but "resolved"
38//!   means something slightly different for each:
39//!     - **BIG = confirmed-resolution-only**: only a confirmed `Some` from the
40//!       `Index.db` raw-key lookup is inserted, so an absent key is never cached and
41//!       the cache simply misses (authoritative absence).
42//!     - **BTI = trie-hit-including-candidates**: any trie HIT is cached, which
43//!       includes prefix-collision candidates — an offset that may belong to a
44//!       different or even absent key — so an absent key CAN receive a cache entry
45//!       pointing at its candidate offset. This is not a correctness bug: the caller
46//!       (`bti_point_lookup`) re-verifies the key bytes at the resolved offset, and a
47//!       cache hit returns the SAME candidate offset a fresh descent returns, so
48//!       re-verification reaches the identical conclusion (mirrors the C3
49//!       `bti_lookup_memo`, which likewise stores `Some(offset)` for a candidate). A
50//!       trie MISS is never cached.
51//! - **Poison-tolerant** (D3): every lock uses `lock().unwrap_or_else(|e|
52//!   e.into_inner())` so one panicking thread cannot wedge the cache. No
53//!   `unwrap()`/`expect()`.
54//! - **No-heuristics** (mandate #28): the key is the authoritative partition-key
55//!   bytes the index/trie is itself keyed on — never inferred from byte content.
56
57use lru::LruCache;
58use std::hash::{Hash, Hasher};
59use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicU64, Ordering};
60use std::sync::Mutex;
61
62/// Approximate per-entry byte overhead ON TOP OF the key's own `len()` bytes.
63///
64/// An entry is a `Box<[u8]>` key plus its [`PartitionLoc`] value, held in an
65/// `LruCache` intrusive-list node. This const covers everything except the key's
66/// payload bytes (which are charged separately via `key.len()`):
67/// - the `Box<[u8]>` fat pointer (16 B) + heap-allocation header/rounding for the
68///   key's own allocation,
69/// - the [`PartitionLoc`] value stored inline in the node (12 B),
70/// - the `LruCache` node itself (a `HashMap` bucket slot + two `NonNull` sibling
71///   links) and the map's load-factor slack.
72///
73/// Rounded generously to 64 B so the byte accounting OVER-estimates rather than
74/// under-estimates true resident memory (the budget must never be silently
75/// exceeded). This makes [`entry_cost`] a conservative upper bound.
76const PER_ENTRY_OVERHEAD: usize = 64;
77
78/// Approximate resident cost of caching one entry whose key is `key_len` bytes:
79/// the key's own payload plus the fixed [`PER_ENTRY_OVERHEAD`]. This is the unit
80/// the per-shard byte budget is enforced against, so a shard holds fewer large-key
81/// entries and more small-key entries — the resident BYTES stay bounded regardless
82/// of key size, which is the whole point of a byte budget over a count cap.
83#[inline]
84const fn entry_cost(key_len: usize) -> usize {
85    key_len.saturating_add(PER_ENTRY_OVERHEAD)
86}
87
88/// Default **per-reader** key-cache BYTE budget.
89///
90/// This cache is per-reader (design D2): each open SSTable reader owns one, so the
91/// resident memory that matters for the `<128MB` budget is the **aggregate** across
92/// every concurrently-open reader. There is no global ceiling across readers, so
93/// this per-reader budget must be chosen so a generous open-reader count stays
94/// comfortably within budget.
95///
96/// # Why bytes, not an entry count (the #1570 roborev fix)
97///
98/// The previous bound was an entry *count* (`4096`/reader). Partition keys are
99/// variable-length (composite/text keys run to Cassandra's ~64 KB limit), so a
100/// count cap does NOT bound resident *bytes*: worst case `~40 readers × 4096
101/// entries × ~1 KB keys ≈ 160 MB` — over the hard `<128MB` budget. The `~80 B/entry`
102/// math the count cap assumed only holds for small (UUID-sized) keys. Bounding by
103/// bytes makes the aggregate footprint **independent of key size**.
104///
105/// # Aggregate-footprint math (byte-bounded, key-size-independent)
106///
107/// With a per-reader budget `B` and `N` concurrently-open readers the aggregate
108/// resident footprint is `≈ N × B` for typical (small) keys, because each reader's
109/// cache evicts to stay within `B` bytes. This is an approximation, not an exact
110/// cap: the eviction guard never evicts the just-resolved entry (the `lru.len() > 1`
111/// condition), so a shard may exceed its per-shard budget by at most **one**
112/// oversized entry. With `shard_count = 16` per reader and a Cassandra partition key
113/// up to ~64 KB, each of the 16 shards can retain one ~64 KB entry beyond its 32 KiB
114/// per-shard budget, so a single reader's true worst case is ~1 MB (~2× the nominal
115/// 512 KiB). The exact upper bound is therefore
116/// `N × (B + shard_count × max_key_bytes)`; the figures below are the **typical**
117/// small-key case, which dominates in practice.
118///
119/// - `B = 512 KiB` per reader.
120/// - A point-read-heavy workload with ~40 open generations (typical keys):
121///   `40 × 512 KiB ≈ 20 MB` — well within `<128MB`, leaving the majority for B1's
122///   decompressed-chunk cache and the working set.
123/// - Even a very generous ~128 open readers is `≈ 128 × 512 KiB = 64 MB` for typical
124///   keys, still within budget. The typical footprint no longer depends on whether
125///   keys are 16 B UUIDs or 1 KB composites — the byte budget bounds it either way,
126///   with the bounded oversized-entry slack above as the only exception.
127///
128/// Each shard's bucket array still grows only with actual occupancy (unbounded
129/// `LruCache` + manual byte-budget eviction), so an idle/empty reader's cache costs
130/// ~nothing; the budget bounds only the fully-occupied worst case.
131///
132/// A single **global bounded cache** keyed on `(sstable_id, key)` (Cassandra's
133/// key-cache model) would bound the aggregate regardless of reader count and is
134/// noted as a deferred future optimization (see `design.md` "Deferred"); it is a
135/// larger architectural change beyond B4's audit-approved per-reader scope.
136pub const DEFAULT_KEY_CACHE_BYTES: usize = 512 * 1024;
137
138/// Default shard count (power of two), mirroring [`DecompressedChunkCache`]'s
139/// `DEFAULT_SHARDS`.
140///
141/// [`DecompressedChunkCache`]: super::DecompressedChunkCache
142pub const DEFAULT_KEY_CACHE_SHARDS: usize = 16;
143
144/// The resolved location of a partition, exactly what the index/trie descent
145/// produces.
146///
147/// BIG (`Index.db`) resolves both fields. BTI resolves only `data_offset` (the
148/// partition's size is bounded later via the successor offset), so a BTI wiring
149/// site stores `data_size = 0` and reads back only `data_offset`. A reader is
150/// exactly one format, so the two never mix within one cache.
151#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
152pub struct PartitionLoc {
153    /// Uncompressed `Data.db` offset the descent resolved.
154    pub data_offset: u64,
155    /// Partition byte size (BIG only; `0` for BTI, which bounds size elsewhere).
156    pub data_size: u32,
157}
158
159impl PartitionLoc {
160    /// Location with a known size (BIG `Index.db` resolution).
161    #[inline]
162    pub fn new(data_offset: u64, data_size: u32) -> Self {
163        Self {
164            data_offset,
165            data_size,
166        }
167    }
168
169    /// Location with only an offset (BTI trie resolution; `data_size = 0`).
170    #[inline]
171    pub fn offset_only(data_offset: u64) -> Self {
172        Self {
173            data_offset,
174            data_size: 0,
175        }
176    }
177}

179/// One cache shard: an `unbounded` `LruCache` mapping the raw partition-key bytes
180/// to the resolved [`PartitionLoc`], plus a running resident-byte counter. The
181/// byte budget is enforced manually on insert (`pop_lru` while over budget) so the
182/// bucket array grows only with occupancy.
183struct Shard {
184    lru: LruCache<Box<[u8]>, PartitionLoc>,
185    /// Sum of [`entry_cost`] over the shard's resident entries. Maintained on every
186    /// insert, in-place replacement, and eviction.
187    current_bytes: usize,
188}
189
190impl Shard {
191    fn new() -> Self {
192        Self {
193            // Used UNBOUNDED by count; the byte budget is enforced explicitly in
194            // `insert` via `pop_lru`. `LruCache::unbounded` never evicts on its own.
195            lru: LruCache::unbounded(),
196            current_bytes: 0,
197        }
198    }
199}
200
201/// A bounded, sharded key→partition-offset cache.
202pub struct KeyOffsetCache {
203    shards: Box<[Mutex<Shard>]>,
204    /// Approximate BYTE budget PER shard. Enforced manually in
205    /// [`insert`](Self::insert) (`pop_lru` while over budget) since each shard is an
206    /// `unbounded` `LruCache`. Always `>= entry_cost(0)` for an enabled cache so a
207    /// shard can always retain one just-resolved entry; `0` when
208    /// [`disabled`](Self::disabled).
209    per_shard_bytes: usize,
210    /// `shards.len() - 1`; `shards.len()` is always a power of two.
211    mask: usize,
212    /// When `true` this is a genuine no-op cache (honoring
213    /// `config.memory.block_cache.enabled == false`): `get` always misses and
214    /// `insert` never retains, so reads bypass the cache entirely.
215    disabled: bool,
216    hits: AtomicU64,
217    misses: AtomicU64,
218    /// Cumulative count of entries evicted to stay within the byte budget
219    /// (issue #1571, B5). Relaxed atomic — advisory observability only.
220    evictions: AtomicU64,
221}
222
223impl std::fmt::Debug for KeyOffsetCache {
224    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
225        f.debug_struct("KeyOffsetCache")
226            .field("shards", &self.shards.len())
227            .field("per_shard_bytes", &self.per_shard_bytes)
228            .field("disabled", &self.disabled)
229            .field("len", &self.len())
230            .field("resident_bytes", &self.resident_bytes())
231            .field("hits", &self.hits.load(Ordering::Relaxed))
232            .field("misses", &self.misses.load(Ordering::Relaxed))
233            .field("evictions", &self.evictions.load(Ordering::Relaxed))
234            .finish()
235    }
236}

238/// A point-in-time snapshot of one key cache's real observability counters
239/// (issue #1571, B5). Summed across live readers to build the process-level
240/// key-cache aggregate reported through `Database::stats().memory_stats`. Every
241/// field is a real counter/aggregate read from the live cache — never a
242/// fabricated placeholder.
243#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, Default)]
244pub(crate) struct KeyCacheSnapshot {
245    pub hits: u64,
246    pub misses: u64,
247    pub evictions: u64,
248    pub resident_bytes: usize,
249    pub capacity_bytes: usize,
250}
251
252impl KeyOffsetCache {
253    /// Create a cache with `total_budget_bytes` split across
254    /// [`DEFAULT_KEY_CACHE_SHARDS`] shards.
255    pub fn with_budget_bytes(total_budget_bytes: usize) -> Self {
256        Self::with_budget_and_shards(total_budget_bytes, DEFAULT_KEY_CACHE_SHARDS)
257    }
258
259    /// Create a cache with `total_budget_bytes` split across `shard_count` shards.
260    ///
261    /// `shard_count` is rounded UP to the next power of two (min 1) so shard
262    /// selection can mask instead of modulo. Unit tests use `shard_count = 1` for
263    /// deterministic eviction ordering; production uses [`DEFAULT_KEY_CACHE_SHARDS`].
264    pub fn with_budget_and_shards(total_budget_bytes: usize, shard_count: usize) -> Self {
265        let shard_count = shard_count.max(1).next_power_of_two();
266        // At least one minimal entry per shard so the cache can always retain the
267        // entry it just resolved. Each shard is an `unbounded` `LruCache` whose
268        // bucket array grows with actual occupancy; the budget is enforced manually
269        // on insert.
270        let per_shard_bytes = (total_budget_bytes / shard_count).max(entry_cost(0));
271        let mut shards = Vec::with_capacity(shard_count);
272        for _ in 0..shard_count {
273            shards.push(Mutex::new(Shard::new()));
274        }
275        Self {
276            shards: shards.into_boxed_slice(),
277            per_shard_bytes,
278            mask: shard_count - 1,
279            disabled: false,
280            hits: AtomicU64::new(0),
281            misses: AtomicU64::new(0),
282            evictions: AtomicU64::new(0),
283        }
284    }
285
286    /// Create a genuine no-op cache (honoring `block_cache.enabled == false`):
287    /// reads bypass it entirely. [`get`](Self::get) always returns `None` (no
288    /// counters touched), [`insert`](Self::insert) retains nothing, and
289    /// `len()`/`budget_bytes()`/`resident_bytes()` all report `0`.
290    pub fn disabled() -> Self {
291        Self {
292            // One dummy shard so shard indexing stays valid; nothing is ever stored.
293            shards: vec![Mutex::new(Shard::new())].into_boxed_slice(),
294            per_shard_bytes: 0,
295            mask: 0,
296            disabled: true,
297            hits: AtomicU64::new(0),
298            misses: AtomicU64::new(0),
299            evictions: AtomicU64::new(0),
300        }
301    }
302
303    /// Poison-tolerant lock: recover the guard if a prior holder panicked, so a
304    /// single panic cannot turn the cache into a panic-for-everyone (design D3).
305    #[inline]
306    fn lock(m: &Mutex<Shard>) -> std::sync::MutexGuard<'_, Shard> {
307        m.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner())
308    }
309
310    #[inline]
311    fn shard_for(&self, key: &[u8]) -> &Mutex<Shard> {
312        let mut h = std::collections::hash_map::DefaultHasher::new();
313        key.hash(&mut h);
314        let idx = (h.finish() as usize) & self.mask;
315        // `idx <= mask < shards.len()`, so this index is always in bounds.
316        &self.shards[idx]
317    }
318
319    /// Look up a partition location by its raw key bytes. On a hit this bumps
320    /// recency and returns the stored [`PartitionLoc`]; on a miss returns `None`.
321    pub fn get(&self, key: &[u8]) -> Option<PartitionLoc> {
322        // A disabled cache never holds anything, so reads bypass it without
323        // touching the hit/miss counters.
324        if self.disabled {
325            return None;
326        }
327        let mut guard = Self::lock(self.shard_for(key));
328        match guard.lru.get(key) {
329            Some(loc) => {
330                let loc = *loc;
331                drop(guard);
332                self.hits.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
333                Some(loc)
334            }
335            None => {
336                drop(guard);
337                self.misses.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
338                None
339            }
340        }
341    }
342
343    /// Insert `loc` under the raw partition-key bytes `key`. On a disabled cache
344    /// this is a no-op. The owning shard evicts LRU entries until it is within its
345    /// per-shard byte budget (never evicting the just-inserted MRU entry).
346    pub fn insert(&self, key: &[u8], loc: PartitionLoc) {
347        if self.disabled {
348            return;
349        }
350        let cost = entry_cost(key.len());
351        let mut guard = Self::lock(self.shard_for(key));
352
353        // Each shard is an `unbounded` `LruCache`, so `put` never evicts: it inserts
354        // (or updates in place) and promotes the key to most-recently-used. Replacing
355        // an existing key reclaims the old entry's byte weight first — the key bytes
356        // are identical, so `cost` is the same for old and new, but subtract-then-add
357        // keeps the counter exact and matches the sibling chunk cache's discipline.
358        if guard.lru.put(Box::from(key), loc).is_some() {
359            guard.current_bytes = guard.current_bytes.saturating_sub(cost);
360        }
361        guard.current_bytes = guard.current_bytes.saturating_add(cost);
362
363        // Evict LRU entries until within the byte budget. The just-inserted key is
364        // now most-recently-used, so `pop_lru` never targets it while other entries
365        // remain. The `len() > 1` guard keeps the entry we just resolved resident
366        // even if it alone exceeds the budget (documented: single oversized entry).
367        let mut evicted_here: u64 = 0;
368        while guard.current_bytes > self.per_shard_bytes && guard.lru.len() > 1 {
369            match guard.lru.pop_lru() {
370                Some((evicted_key, _)) => {
371                    let reclaimed = entry_cost(evicted_key.len());
372                    guard.current_bytes = guard.current_bytes.saturating_sub(reclaimed);
373                    evicted_here += 1;
374                }
375                None => break,
376            }
377        }
378        drop(guard);
379        if evicted_here > 0 {
380            self.evictions.fetch_add(evicted_here, Ordering::Relaxed);
381        }
382    }
383
384    /// Total resident entry count across all shards.
385    pub fn len(&self) -> usize {
386        self.shards.iter().map(|m| Self::lock(m).lru.len()).sum()
387    }
388
389    /// Whether the cache currently holds no entries.
390    pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
391        self.len() == 0
392    }
393
394    /// Total approximate resident bytes across all shards (sum of [`entry_cost`]
395    /// over resident entries). A [`disabled`](Self::disabled) no-op cache reports
396    /// `0`.
397    pub fn resident_bytes(&self) -> usize {
398        self.shards
399            .iter()
400            .map(|m| Self::lock(m).current_bytes)
401            .sum()
402    }
403
404    /// The configured total byte budget (`per_shard_bytes × shard count`). A
405    /// [`disabled`](Self::disabled) no-op cache reports `0`.
406    pub fn budget_bytes(&self) -> usize {
407        self.per_shard_bytes.saturating_mul(self.shards.len())
408    }
409
410    /// Cumulative cache hits (test/observability instrumentation).
411    pub fn hit_count(&self) -> u64 {
412        self.hits.load(Ordering::Relaxed)
413    }
414
415    /// Cumulative cache misses (test/observability instrumentation).
416    pub fn miss_count(&self) -> u64 {
417        self.misses.load(Ordering::Relaxed)
418    }
419
420    /// Cumulative entries evicted to stay within budget (issue #1571, B5).
421    ///
422    /// Real relaxed-atomic counter; a [`disabled`](Self::disabled) no-op cache
423    /// never evicts and reports `0`.
424    pub fn eviction_count(&self) -> u64 {
425        self.evictions.load(Ordering::Relaxed)
426    }
427
428    /// A point-in-time snapshot of this cache's real observability counters,
429    /// summed across readers to build the process-level key-cache aggregate
430    /// (issue #1571, B5). Reads only relaxed atomics plus the per-shard locks
431    /// occupancy already uses — no new hot-path lock.
432    pub(crate) fn snapshot(&self) -> KeyCacheSnapshot {
433        KeyCacheSnapshot {
434            hits: self.hit_count(),
435            misses: self.miss_count(),
436            evictions: self.eviction_count(),
437            resident_bytes: self.resident_bytes(),
438            capacity_bytes: self.budget_bytes(),
439        }
440    }
441}
442
443impl Default for KeyOffsetCache {
444    fn default() -> Self {
445        Self::with_budget_bytes(DEFAULT_KEY_CACHE_BYTES)
446    }
447}

449#[cfg(test)]
450mod tests {
451    use super::*;
452    use std::sync::Arc;
453
454    /// A budget that holds exactly `n` entries whose keys are `key_len` bytes each,
455    /// on a single shard (so eviction is deterministic — no wall-clock, no shard
456    /// spread). Used to make byte-budget eviction assertions exact.
457    fn budget_for(n: usize, key_len: usize) -> usize {
458        entry_cost(key_len) * n
459    }
460
461    /// Task 1.1: eviction order — single shard sized for exactly 2 entries; insert
462    /// A, insert B, access A, insert C → B (LRU) evicted, A and C survive.
463    #[test]
464    fn eviction_order_lru_single_shard() {
465        // All keys are 5 bytes ("key-X"), so 2 entries' worth of byte budget holds
466        // exactly two of them.
467        let cache = KeyOffsetCache::with_budget_and_shards(budget_for(2, 5), 1);
468        let a = b"key-A".as_slice();
469        let b = b"key-B".as_slice();
470        let c = b"key-C".as_slice();
471
472        cache.insert(a, PartitionLoc::new(10, 100));
473        cache.insert(b, PartitionLoc::new(20, 200));
474        // Access A so it becomes more-recently-used than B.
475        assert_eq!(cache.get(a), Some(PartitionLoc::new(10, 100)));
476        // Insert C: over budget → evict the LRU, which is now B.
477        cache.insert(c, PartitionLoc::new(30, 300));
478
479        assert_eq!(
480            cache.get(a),
481            Some(PartitionLoc::new(10, 100)),
482            "A (recently used) must survive"
483        );
484        assert_eq!(
485            cache.get(c),
486            Some(PartitionLoc::new(30, 300)),
487            "C (just inserted) must survive"
488        );
489        assert_eq!(
490            cache.get(b),
491            None,
492            "B (least recently used) must be evicted"
493        );
494        assert_eq!(cache.len(), 2);
495        assert!(cache.resident_bytes() <= cache.budget_bytes());
496    }
497
498    /// Issue #1571 (B5): the eviction counter reflects the real number of entries
499    /// evicted to stay within budget; the snapshot exposes the real numbers, and a
500    /// disabled cache reports honest zeros.
501    #[test]
502    fn eviction_count_and_snapshot_track_real_activity() {
503        // Single shard sized for exactly 2 five-byte keys.
504        let cache = KeyOffsetCache::with_budget_and_shards(budget_for(2, 5), 1);
505        assert_eq!(cache.eviction_count(), 0);
506
507        cache.insert(b"key-A".as_slice(), PartitionLoc::new(10, 100));
508        cache.insert(b"key-B".as_slice(), PartitionLoc::new(20, 200));
509        assert_eq!(cache.eviction_count(), 0, "still within budget");
510
511        // Each further distinct insert evicts exactly one LRU entry.
512        cache.insert(b"key-C".as_slice(), PartitionLoc::new(30, 300));
513        assert_eq!(cache.eviction_count(), 1);
514        cache.insert(b"key-D".as_slice(), PartitionLoc::new(40, 400));
515        assert_eq!(cache.eviction_count(), 2);
516
517        // One hit + one miss so the snapshot carries real counter values.
518        assert!(cache.get(b"key-D".as_slice()).is_some());
519        assert!(cache.get(b"absent".as_slice()).is_none());
520        let snap = cache.snapshot();
521        assert_eq!(snap.evictions, 2);
522        assert_eq!(snap.hits, 1);
523        assert_eq!(snap.misses, 1);
524        assert_eq!(snap.resident_bytes, cache.resident_bytes());
525        assert_eq!(snap.capacity_bytes, cache.budget_bytes());
526
527        // A disabled cache never evicts and reports honest zeros.
528        let disabled = KeyOffsetCache::disabled();
529        disabled.insert(b"k".as_slice(), PartitionLoc::new(1, 1));
530        let dsnap = disabled.snapshot();
531        assert_eq!(dsnap.evictions, 0);
532        assert_eq!(dsnap.resident_bytes, 0);
533        assert_eq!(dsnap.capacity_bytes, 0);
534    }
535
536    /// Task 1.2: BYTE bound — inserting more distinct equal-size keys than the
537    /// budget holds keeps resident bytes within the budget after every insert.
538    #[test]
539    fn resident_bytes_bounded() {
540        // Budget for exactly 4 entries whose keys are 6 bytes ("key-NN").
541        let key_len = 6;
542        let cache = KeyOffsetCache::with_budget_and_shards(budget_for(4, key_len), 1);
543        for i in 0..50u64 {
544            let key = format!("key-{i:02}");
545            assert_eq!(key.len(), key_len, "test assumes fixed-width keys");
546            cache.insert(key.as_bytes(), PartitionLoc::new(i, i as u32));
547            assert!(
548                cache.resident_bytes() <= cache.budget_bytes(),
549                "resident {} exceeded budget {} after insert {}",
550                cache.resident_bytes(),
551                cache.budget_bytes(),
552                i
553            );
554            assert!(
555                cache.len() <= 4,
556                "resident count exceeded 4 after insert {i}"
557            );
558        }
559    }
560
561    /// Byte-budget eviction is key-SIZE aware: a large key costs more budget, so a
562    /// shard sized for a handful of small keys holds fewer large keys. This is the
563    /// property the count cap lacked (the #1570 fix).
564    #[test]
565    fn large_keys_evict_sooner_than_small_keys() {
566        // Budget = room for exactly 4 small (4-byte) keys.
567        let small_len = 4;
568        let budget = budget_for(4, small_len);
569        let cache = KeyOffsetCache::with_budget_and_shards(budget, 1);
570
571        // Each large key costs `entry_cost(budget/2) = budget/2 + PER_ENTRY_OVERHEAD`,
572        // so any two of them together exceed the shard budget (one fits, two do not).
573        let big = vec![b'x'; budget / 2];
574        let mut big1 = big.clone();
575        big1[0] = b'a';
576        let mut big2 = big.clone();
577        big2[0] = b'b';
578        cache.insert(&big1, PartitionLoc::new(1, 1));
579        cache.insert(&big2, PartitionLoc::new(2, 2));
580
581        // Both large keys cannot be resident at once under the byte budget, so the
582        // LRU (big1) is evicted — a count cap of 4 would have kept both.
583        assert!(cache.resident_bytes() <= cache.budget_bytes());
584        assert_eq!(cache.get(&big1), None, "LRU large key must be evicted");
585        assert_eq!(cache.get(&big2), Some(PartitionLoc::new(2, 2)));
586    }
587
588    /// Task 1.3: a hit returns the stored location; a different key never aliases;
589    /// a never-inserted key misses (parity / no-fabrication).
590    #[test]
591    fn hit_returns_stored_location_no_alias() {
592        let cache = KeyOffsetCache::with_budget_and_shards(DEFAULT_KEY_CACHE_BYTES, 1);
593        let a = b"partition-A".as_slice();
594        let b = b"partition-B".as_slice();
595        cache.insert(a, PartitionLoc::new(63, 512));
596        cache.insert(b, PartitionLoc::new(125, 256));
597
598        assert_eq!(cache.get(a), Some(PartitionLoc::new(63, 512)));
599        assert_eq!(cache.get(b), Some(PartitionLoc::new(125, 256)));
600        assert_eq!(
601            cache.get(b"never-inserted".as_slice()),
602            None,
603            "a never-inserted key must miss (no fabricated hit)"
604        );
605    }
606
607    /// Re-inserting the same key must not double-count its bytes (in-place
608    /// replacement subtracts the old cost before adding the new).
609    #[test]
610    fn reinsert_same_key_does_not_grow_resident_bytes() {
611        let cache = KeyOffsetCache::with_budget_and_shards(DEFAULT_KEY_CACHE_BYTES, 1);
612        let k = b"stable-key".as_slice();
613        cache.insert(k, PartitionLoc::new(1, 1));
614        let after_first = cache.resident_bytes();
615        cache.insert(k, PartitionLoc::new(2, 2));
616        cache.insert(k, PartitionLoc::new(3, 3));
617        assert_eq!(cache.len(), 1, "re-insert must not add a second entry");
618        assert_eq!(
619            cache.resident_bytes(),
620            after_first,
621            "re-inserting the same key must not grow resident bytes"
622        );
623        assert_eq!(cache.get(k), Some(PartitionLoc::new(3, 3)));
624    }

626    /// Task 1.4: `disabled()` is a genuine no-op (get misses, insert retains
627    /// nothing, occupancy + byte counters report zero).
628    #[test]
629    fn disabled_cache_is_a_genuine_no_op() {
630        let cache = KeyOffsetCache::disabled();
631        assert_eq!(cache.budget_bytes(), 0);
632
633        cache.insert(b"k".as_slice(), PartitionLoc::new(1, 2));
634        assert_eq!(
635            cache.get(b"k".as_slice()),
636            None,
637            "disabled cache never retains"
638        );
639        assert_eq!(cache.len(), 0);
640        assert_eq!(cache.resident_bytes(), 0);
641        assert!(cache.is_empty());
642        assert_eq!(cache.hit_count(), 0);
643        assert_eq!(cache.miss_count(), 0);
644    }

646    /// Task 1.5: poison recovery — a panic while holding a shard lock must not
647    /// wedge the cache; subsequent get/insert recover the guard and continue.
648    #[test]
649    fn poisoned_lock_recovers() {
650        use std::panic::{catch_unwind, AssertUnwindSafe};
651        use std::thread;
652
653        let cache = Arc::new(KeyOffsetCache::with_budget_and_shards(
654            DEFAULT_KEY_CACHE_BYTES,
655            1,
656        ));
657        cache.insert(b"k".as_slice(), PartitionLoc::new(7, 8));
658
659        // Poison the single shard's mutex by panicking while holding it.
660        let poison_cache = Arc::clone(&cache);
661        let _ = thread::spawn(move || {
662            let _guard = KeyOffsetCache::lock(&poison_cache.shards[0]);
663            panic!("intentional poison");
664        })
665        .join();
666
667        let res = catch_unwind(AssertUnwindSafe(|| {
668            let hit = cache.get(b"k".as_slice());
669            cache.insert(b"k2".as_slice(), PartitionLoc::new(9, 10));
670            hit
671        }));
672        assert_eq!(
673            res.ok(),
674            Some(Some(PartitionLoc::new(7, 8))),
675            "cache must recover from a poisoned lock"
676        );
677    }
678
679    #[test]
680    fn shard_count_rounds_to_power_of_two() {
681        let cache = KeyOffsetCache::with_budget_and_shards(DEFAULT_KEY_CACHE_BYTES, 10);
682        assert_eq!(cache.shards.len(), 16);
683        assert_eq!(cache.mask, 15);
684    }
